festivals: Mallikarjuna Temple festival (5 days in March)

history.summary: Hindu Shiva temple in the heart of Kasaragod city, near the taluk office, with the Kumbala (Chandragiri) river flowing close by to the south. Legend says the Shiva idol was adorned by Arjuna of the Mahabharata. The temple was built by the Ikkeri kings to serve warriors brought from Karnataka; after a long period of neglect the site had to be shifted in 1977 when temple lands were acquired for the railway line, and the sreekovil, namaskara mandapam, chuttambalam and other structures were rebuilt by a renovation committee, with the compound wall completed in 1985. The valiyambalam walls carry modern paintings of Sankaracharya, Ayyappa, Ganapathi, Shiva and Durga; the maryaada arches recall Arjuna's archery.

town_description: Kasaragod is the northernmost coastal town of Kerala and headquarters of Kasaragod district, about 50 km south of Mangalore. An old trading port of the Kolathunadu region, it was ruled successively by the Ikkeri Nayakas, Mysore and the British. The town is known for Bekal Fort, Chandragiri Fort, the Theyyam ritual art and Yakshagana, and sits in one of India's rare districts where seven languages - Malayalam, Tulu, Kannada, Konkani, Beary and others - are widely spoken.
